source.title: SAEs Discover Meaningful Features in the IOI Task

record.file_problem: The text is intact, but the referenced plots are not included, so their plotted values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: Uses the IOI circuit and its supervised features as a benchmark and set of sites for SAE steering experiments, but does not test whether the circuit is complete, minimal, or responsible for ordinary IOI performance.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for feature edits and next-token predictions at IOI circuit sites. These are SAE-steering results, not tests of the 26-head circuit's faithfulness, completeness, minimality, or stated head roles. It does not test backup-head self-repair, circuit transfer across models, or the circuit-evaluation sensitivities in the claim versions. Referenced plots have no numerical values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Uses the IOI circuit's sites (e.g. (B)NM out, S-I out) as locations for evaluating SAE feature edits against supervised features. It reports SAE steering performance, not tests of the circuit's faithfulness, completeness, minimality, head roles, backup behaviour, transfer, method dependence or prompt-variant robustness.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAEs trained on IOI data, with better training and selection, nearly match supervised features for steering; gated beat vanilla, topk beat gated in most cases; sparsity correlates more with edit success than loss recovered.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates SAE feature editing and activation patching against supervised feature edits, rather than finding and testing the IOI circuit through circuit ablations and patching.
record.method_sensitivity: Edit accuracy varies with SAE architecture and editing method; the topk comparison also reports an exception for interpretation-aware editing of IO.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2 small IOI circuit sites, SAE features (gated, topk) nearly match supervised IO/S/Pos features for steering edits; vanilla SAEs lag.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised SAE features at IOI circuit sites can steer IOI attributes nearly as well as supervised conditional-mean features.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE sparsity correlates more with edit success than logit-difference recovered; SAE features resemble supervised IO features more than Pos features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE sparsity predicts steering usefulness better than loss recovered on IOI.

record.problems: The supplied text omits the referenced plots and their numerical values. Uncertainty estimates are not stated. The authors note they did not ablate the training ingredients to determine which caused the improved results; their edit-distance measure is a proxy for downstream performance.

untested.parts: 26 heads, 7 classes, faithfulness/completeness/minimality not tested; circuit sites only used as edit locations.
No ablation of name movers or backup self-repair measured.
Only GPT-2 small; no other models, checkpoints or tasks.
No circuit faithfulness/completeness evaluation under varying ablations or metrics.
No tests across templates, name orders or more names (Pos attribute edited only as a feature).

missing.what: Footnote claim: attention-score decomposition into feature interactions is consistent with Wang et al's algorithm 'with some twists'; cited from the arXiv paper, not shown here.
missing.versions: V1 (cited result, not tested in this post)

record.verdict_notes: Plots not in text, so no numerical values. Results on circuit validity come only by citation to the companion arXiv paper (2405.08366). This is a blog post on the Alignment Forum and is not peer-reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the 26-head circuit, its seven classes, or faithfulness, completeness, and minimality.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads or test self-repair by backup heads.
Does not test whether the same circuit carries IOI in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or circuit-evaluation metrics.
Does not test how circuit faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation, metric, or prompt distribution.
Does not test circuit components across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Patched SAE-edited activations at IOI circuit sites and compared next-token predictions with the ground-truth counterfactual edit.
rows.baseline: Supervised feature edit; no-intervention baseline also shown
rows.value: The text says gated SAEs match or outperform supervised edit accuracy more successfully than vanilla SAEs; vanilla SAEs lag significantly in edit accuracy. Numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The article describes the direction of the comparison but supplies no plotted values in the provided text. This is an SAE-editing result, not a test of the circuit claim.
rows.check: SAE method-comparison result (the study's own method vs supervised edits), not a measure of any circuit version; no values in text.
